## 2026/09/23

### Reading - K. Nandra (2007) @nandra_xmm-newton_2007

- Covers 37 observations of 26 Seyfert galaxies from XMM-Newton  
    - All show Iron K emission, which makes this paper useful for candidate selection for our research
    - Around 45% of the data was best fit with a relativistically blurred reflection model
        - Some objects may not show the broadening?
- General background information
    - Iron line emission broadening predicted in Fabian et al (1989)
    - This was alongside the discovery that the emission likely comes from the accretion disk
    - Useful reads?
        - Fabian (1989)
        - George, Nandra & Fabian (1990)
        - Tanaka et al. (1995)
- Data Reduction
    - They give a lot of detail on their data reduction which may be useful further down the line
    - Source taken from a circle with radius 700 detector pixels
    - There are several windowing modes on the CCD which will be important to note
- Model
    - They found that the minimum set of models was:
        - Power law continuum (modelling the corona)
        - Reflection model (e.g. XILLVER)
        - Can use relativistic blurring on this however not necessarily needed
        - Ionized absorber model
    - The models used are covered in depth, including how they selected if and how to apply the absorber models
        - This will be useful later down the line to give some direction when fitting
    - They modelled the emission using a broad and narrow component, this may be useful to consider?
- Potential candiadate list (from Figure 3 of Nandra et al.)
    - NGC3516(2)
        - Very broad emission centred around the Fe K$\alpha$ line
    - NGC3783(2)
        - Quite a clean spectrum with low noise/small errors
    - NGC4151(2) or NGC4151(3)
        - Clean spectrum with broad emission
